findings: Supplemental source review for upstream a7a526b: Select.Stepper and SelectStepper are the same public component identity. It did not exist in the historical 230-identity performance report; that report supplies no timing or bundle evidence for this component.

The visible previous/value/next control is fixed-size, but every supplied item is emitted as a native select option. Current-value lookup, adjacent enabled-item lookup and native-value validation are linear scans; missing-value reverse navigation and End can copy/reverse the items. No option-count bound or virtualization is claimed, and no measured performance rewrite is asserted.

Controlled and uncontrolled values retain native form projection. The single form-reset listener is keyed by controlled mode/form, reads current item/default/value refs, and removes the listener and pending timeout on cleanup. Disabled/read-only guards, skipped disabled options, loop boundaries and RTL key mapping were reviewed.

findings: Progress updated one item but reconstructed every row's expensive control/surface subtree. Extracted a memoized row and stabilized labels/actions while retaining latest callbacks via existing refs. Tests cover unrelated rows, same item identity, every progress notification, cancellation/late callbacks, and disabled/label changes. The parent still traverses the file list for ordered immutable updates.

Changed Upload items must replace the changed item objects, normally in a replacement files array; same-reference in-place item mutation is intentionally unsupported by memoized rows. Individual label override values are dependencies, so same-object label edits/deletion and new-but-equivalent override objects remain supported and runtime-tested.
